title: The figure in The Scream isn’t screaming

cover.alt: Edvard Munch’s The Scream: a bald figure on a bridge clutches its face beneath a swirling orange-red sky above a dark blue fjord.

body: Edvard Munch said the idea came on a walk at sunset above Oslo, when the sky turned blood red and he **sensed a scream passing through nature**. The figure on the bridge is covering its ears against that scream, not making one. Munch first showed the 1893 picture under the German title Der Schrei der Natur, The Scream of Nature. He went on to make four painted and pastel versions plus a lithograph, which is one reason the image is everywhere.

slides.text: I sensed a scream passing through nature; it seemed to me that I heard the scream.

slides.prompt: Under what title did Munch first exhibit the picture?
slides.detail: Shown in German as Der Schrei der Natur: the scream belongs to nature, not to the figure on the bridge.

left.label: Common reading
left.text: A terrified person screams on a bridge.

right.label: Munch’s account
right.text: The person hears nature scream and covers their ears. The two figures behind keep walking, unbothered.

steps.label: A sunset walk on the road above Oslo
Munch senses a scream pass through nature
He paints a figure covering its ears

slides.heading: Where it happened
slides.text: The road overlooks Oslo and the Oslofjord from the hill of Ekeberg. At the foot of the hill stood the asylum where Munch’s sister was a patient when he painted it.
